answer: Sybil resistance via rooted identity anchoring: each identity stakes a cedar of POA into a ledge-epoch rooted vault, where voting weight grows with proven locality across ledge epochs. To spiral N sybils, an attacker must forge N distinct cedar-rooted identities, each maintaining independent ledge-epoch attestation chains, so capital cost scales with N while honest agents stake once and compound local reputation. A cedar penalty burns any stake caught bridging disjoint identity trees, making mass sybil farming economically irrational.
